turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I was told to come back, because my throat swab came back positive. The nurse phoned me yesterday.
Yes, I've got the result here. Group A strep, a bacterial throat infection. How are you feeling now? ~
A bit better than at the weekend, but my throat is still very sore. And my glands are swollen. ~
When did it start? ~
Five days ago. Fever, headache, and a terrible throat. ~
Any rash, or difficulty swallowing your saliva?
No rash. I can swallow, it just hurts.
What are you taking at the moment?
Just paracetamol, 1 gram, four times a day.
Let me look at your throat. Open wide. ~
Ahh.
Your tonsils are red and swollen with white spots on both, and there are tender swollen glands under your jaw.
It looks bad? ~
It's typical. I'd say this is strep throat, bacterial tonsillitis, as the swab confirms.
Can you give me something? ~
Yes. I'll prescribe penicillin V, 500 mg, four times a day, for ten days.
Ten days? My friend had five. ~
For strep throat, ten days is the full course, to clear it and prevent complications. Finish it all, even if you feel better in two. ~
Okay. ~
Is there anything about the antibiotic you'd like me to explain before we go on? ~
No, that's clear enough. ~
Pulse 82, temperature 37.6, oxygen 98 percent.
Is that all right? ~
Fine. A mild temperature, as expected. Rest, drink plenty, and use paracetamol for the pain. Salt-water gargles help too.
Can I go to work? ~
Stay off until you've had two days of the antibiotic, and your fever has gone.
Right. ~
If you can't swallow, drool, have a very stiff neck, or a one-sided swollen throat, come back at once.
I will. ~
I'd like to see you again in a week, if you're not completely better.
Thanks, doctor. ~
